comments.author: @2CSST2
comments.text:
This new approach of VLA shown here is most definitely a big breakthrough, you glossed quickly over the fact that it can transfer concepts from different situations to new situations, but I think is an extremely important new emergent capability. This is known to be one of the big reasons why the human brain is so flexible/general, or rather intelligent and adaptable. 

You don't need to learn everything from the start when entering a new kitchen, you have a general concept of what a kitchen is and hence immediately know where and how to use the stove, etc. But this is not only useful for analogous situation, but even new situations or intellectual obstacles can be adapted to much more quickly, as you recycle concepts already learned to combine them or mold them to fit to new situations. 

For example learning a new language, although difficult, is made way easier by the parallels you can make with your own language and its mechanics. You can quickly absorb what "fleur" in French means by just knowing it translates to "flower". You also already know the concept of plural, verbs that refer to past, present, future. Even though the mechanics are different in French, they're similar and so it's miles easier than if you knew no language at all, say you were deaf, and had to learn French. 

So now for an AI model to speak different languages it has to be trained with lots of data of all those languages. But imagine if you could just feed it a dictionary and a few books about verbs and so on about a new language, and that model could learn it by itself like we do, except of course millions of times faster. And we're just talking about language as an example, but imagine if the same can be done by giving it books about physics, engineering, etc. This is sort of what LLMs already do, but very slowly and rigidly in a roundabout way through word patterns. Models could learn MUCH more quickly, generally, and flexibly if they could have that concepts transferring ability, this would be another big step towards general intelligence. 

I'm rambling on, I know VLA is just for robots to learn handling motions, but I would claim bringing this technique to any concept in general might be the next big leap forward. This could be the next big change in structure after Transformer, and crazy things would happen once you scale that up to huge new compute like it did for GPT-4 with the Transformer model.
